message.content:
**Triangulation metrics** are the quantitative indicators that describe how well a triangulation run performed.  
In the context of our system they capture the quality, reliability, and usefulness of the triangulation data that has been generated for a product or branch. Typical metrics include:

| Metric | What it measures | Typical interpretation |
|--------|------------------|------------------------|
| **Coverage** | % of the target area that was successfully triangulated | Higher coverage → more complete data |
| **Accuracy** | Mean absolute error between triangulated points and ground‑truth reference points | Lower error → higher precision |
| **Precision** | Variability of repeated triangulations on the same area | Lower variance → more consistent results |
| **Completeness** | % of expected data points that were actually produced | Higher completeness → fewer missing points |
| **Processing time** | Time taken to complete the triangulation run | Faster processing → better performance |
| **Resource usage** | CPU, memory, or GPU consumption during the run | Lower usage → more efficient execution |
| **Error rate** | % of points flagged as outliers or invalid | Lower error rate → cleaner dataset |

These metrics are automatically calculated after each triangulation run and are stored in the database. They can be queried via the API (e.g., `GET /metrics?product_id=…&branch_id=…`) or visualized in the dashboard to monitor performance over time, compare different runs, or trigger alerts when thresholds are breached.
